E01.name: Sudoku architecture comparison: seven models and ten seeds
E01.protocol: Final EMA and per-seed test-peak checkpoints from 70 included runs. The shared-checkpoint HRM evaluation uses the shared step 54,080, not per-seed peaks. HRM/TRM/RT use the historical ten seeds; the other four architectures use the original three plus seven additional seeds.

E02.name: 28-layer fixed-depth Transformer with and without deep supervision
E02.protocol: Three training seeds per model; standard comparisons use test-peak checkpoints. Single-clue experiments instead use terminal EMA checkpoints; see E38.

E03.name: Small models: separate H/L versus deeper or wider shared H/L and RT
E03.protocol: Five groups with three seeds each, trained for 120 epochs. The reference HRM result is 79.58 ± 1.54 using the original three seeds, not the 80.77 variant obtained by replacing seed 2 in the historical README.

E04.name: Two-, three- and four-timescale hierarchies
E04.protocol: Ten seeds each for HRM2/3/4; EMA checkpoints selected at the test peak; 448–9,548 block evaluations. HRM2 is shared with E01.

E05.name: Independent three-seed MLP-Mixer reproduction and inference scaling
E05.protocol: Three independent seeds, fixed final epoch 20; 20,000 test puzzles; 97.49 ± 1.07 at 256 inference cycles. Distinct from the ten-seed Mixer comparison in E01.

E06.name: Final-output-only training versus deep supervision
E06.protocol: HRM/RT × two supervision protocols × three seeds; peak of the mean curve within 80,000 updates; requires complete curves and corresponding EMA checkpoints.

E07.name: RT learning-rate × weight-decay sweep with 24 settings
E07.protocol: One seed; three learning rates × eight weight decays, with 20 evaluation points per run; retain peak and final results.

E08.name: Sudoku training-data scaling at ten sample sizes
E08.protocol: Ten sizes × two models × three seeds = 60 runs; 83,200 updates and 128 inference cycles; test-selected EMA peak and final checkpoints; original seeds 1/2/3.

E09.name: Sudoku model-size scaling at four parameter counts
E09.protocol: The four reported sizes comprise 61 runs and 40 seed groups. Average same-seed reruns first; retain the EMA peak of every included run.

E10.name: Three-seed Sudoku long inference with stable16 stopping
E10.protocol: Three independent training seeds each for HRM/RT, fixed EMA checkpoints selected by test performance at 16 inference cycles, with ties resolved in favor of the later step; shared 1,000-puzzle training sample and 20,000 test puzzles; 16–16,384 inference cycles; 96.76 ± 0.90.

E11.name: Continuous inference and post-solution stability on 4,096 Sudoku puzzles
E11.protocol: One frozen checkpoint each for HRM/TRM/RT, continued through 16,384 inference cycles. No recorded endpoint reversals among the 3,951 puzzles solved by HRM.

E12.name: Deterministic HRM versus stochastic H / HRM+KL across three runs
E12.protocol: Six EMA checkpoints: HRM original epoch 12/repeat 1 epoch 16/repeat 2 epoch 12; KL original epoch 13/repeat 1 epoch 10/repeat 2 epoch 14. Selected by test performance at 128 inference cycles; first-valid stopping up to 4,096 inference cycles.

E13.name: Maze-Hard continuous inference and current/ever-solved stability
E13.protocol: One retrained checkpoint each for HRM/shared-HL/RT; 200 selection and 800 evaluation mazes; up to 16,384 inference cycles.

E14.name: Frontier LLMs on Sudoku and Maze
E14.protocol: API models require no local checkpoint; freeze version, reasoning effort and token cap. Reported results use four models × two tasks × 100 calls = 800 calls; the other 2,400 of 3,200 archived records are historical SAT calls.

E15.name: Qwen Instruct and teacher-CoT supervised fine-tuning
E15.protocol: Frozen Instruct base-model revision and SFT weights/adapters; 256 puzzles × four outputs × two conditions; 939 training traces.

E16.name: Three-seed IRED Extreme-1k baseline
E16.protocol: Three fixed final EMA checkpoints, 50,000 updates, 20,000 + 100 test puzzles; ten energy stages with 20 inner steps each.

E17.name: IRED SAT-Net diagnostics, sampling steps and transfer
E17.protocol: One training seed (42); 50,000-update EMA and two learning-rate continuations to 60,000-update EMA; 20/80/200 inner iterations; selected 60,000-update checkpoint transferred to Extreme.

E18.name: Published SudokuDiT-Extreme-1k result
E18.protocol: Result from external literature/code, not a local training run.

E19.name: Native Sudoku output-board sequence
E19.protocol: The trajectory example uses test_hard row 12145 and 1000_tuned_hrm_new/epoch_19.pt, SHA256 3a535185e4c0b4fcd03ba5c7241198047ed19b5bb5825af09f416ebc49816115. Native 6L→H schedule; record 32 H updates and display through H4.

E20.name: HRM/RT trajectories and two-dimensional constraint-violation landscapes
E20.protocol: HRM case 6566 with 4,096 extended L updates followed by H; RT case 35, seed 3, epoch 5. The HRM landscape uses an L-only probe; RT is scored directly.

E21.name: Case study: update versus retain H from the same L state
E21.protocol: Case 6566 at the H4 boundary; 4,096 L continuation updates plus 32 subsequent native H phases; shares its checkpoint with E19/20.

E22.name: Paired H versus extra-L single-step answer directions on 253 puzzles
E22.protocol: One frozen backbone with a shared linear readout; 800/200 readout training/validation puzzles; 3,360 states from 253 puzzles.

E23.name: H→L versus L→L historical distance and radial step controls on 64 puzzles
E23.protocol: One fixed backbone; 64 puzzles and seven L-phase lengths: 6/9/12/18/24/36/48.

E24.name: MSD across four windows and long lags; shared-weight and equal-frequency ablations
E24.protocol: Three seeds each for HRM/TRM/equal-frequency HRM/RT; 256 puzzles; epoch 19; 21 short lags and 39 long lags.
E24.reproduction_status: Fresh checkpoint-to-MSD collection and statistics; public HF defaults and explicit local checkpoint/cohort overrides.

E25.name: Mixer long-trajectory screening and probe landscapes on the same trajectory
E25.protocol: Screen 32 puzzles × three seeds; display case 11486 from one seed, H1–H8; probe train/validation/test split by time blocks.

E26.name: Four blocks of the local transition Jacobian
E26.protocol: HRM seed 1, epoch 16; 20,000 puzzles, 32 H updates and one random probe per puzzle in FP32.

E27.name: Taylor/Jacobian decomposition along native update directions
E27.protocol: HRM seeds 1/2/3 at epochs 16/19/10; 64 puzzles and 31 boundaries.

E28.name: Conditional microstep stability and contraction before and after solving
E28.protocol: One checkpoint; of 4,096 long-inference puzzles, 145 remain unsolved; the 12 lowest-index unsolved puzzles are continued, leaving 11 unsolved and one solved. The native trajectory uses case 6566.

E29.name: Output sensitivity and memory across inference cycles
E29.protocol: HRM epochs 16/19/10 and RT epochs 4/6/5; three seeds with 10,000 puzzles each; 16 × 16 matrices and 16 output probes.

E30.name: Recovering old H from new L without the H-to-H link
E30.protocol: 13 model conditions at updates 1/8/24; three original models, link deletion/continued training, and no-HH training from scratch. Both backbones and linear/MLP probes are required.
E30.reproduction_status: feature extraction, decoder fit/audit and CPU continuation smoke verified; full source training and 13-condition comparison pending

E31.name: Same-puzzle search geometry: DFS, simulated annealing and HRM; three-seed SA budgets
E31.protocol: SA requires no checkpoint and uses three inference seeds; HRM uses shared frozen weights; 99-frame distance matrices.
E31.reproduction_status: fresh producers and combined records audit available; full-budget successful comparison not rerun

E32.name: Readout of discrete Sudoku constraint violations and CE/MSE
E32.protocol: One frozen checkpoint with H/L/HL OLS readouts; 256/128/128-puzzle split, 192 pre-L states per puzzle; L-only r = .9834.

E33.name: Constraint readout and relative L step size on 1,056 puzzles; frozen-H population curves
E33.protocol: 1000_tuned_hrm_new/epoch_19.pt, SHA256 3a535185…; 1,056 puzzles and 101,376 states, plus a single-puzzle frozen-H example. The freezing protocol updates H every ten L steps, retains 0/1/2/3 H updates, then freezes H through global L step 50. It does not use the 6L/H schedule of other experiments.

E34.name: Fixed-checkpoint comparison of frozen H, Gaussian noise and continued H updates
E34.protocol: One fixed checkpoint and three disjoint cohorts of 1,056 puzzles; sigma .1/.2/.3; 186 accumulated continuation readouts; stochastic results come from E12.

E35.name: Target-dose interventions on the discrete E probe
E35.protocol: 81 development puzzles after H4; clipped L-only E targets of ±5/15/30%, with eight matched random controls.

E36.name: Norm-preserving H/L interventions along CE/MSE directions
E36.protocol: The same 81 puzzles; relative per-token displacements of ±.2/1/3%, both H and L modules, and eight random controls.

E37.name: SAT violated-clause probes and H/L direction interventions
E37.protocol: SAT HRM raw s61440.pt, SHA256 09146cff…; 219/108/108 split; 64 inference cycles and 6,480 intervention branches.

E38.name: Single-clue edits: training/test origins, rearranged cells and copying old answers
E38.protocol: Four models × three seeds, terminal EMA last.pt; 781 training-derived and 886 test-derived pairs.

E39.name: Four-way Sudoku Easy/Hard transfer and peak-selection sensitivity
E39.protocol: Three models × two training difficulty bands × three seeds = 18 runs; reported results use fixed epoch-20 EMA, with a separate test-peak sensitivity analysis over 20 epochs.

E40.name: Kernel quality, generalization capability, symmetries and native cell accuracy
E40.protocol: Three seeds each for HRM/TRM/RT; 8,192 distinct puzzles and 16 × 256 symmetry variants; HRM epochs 16/12/11, TRM epochs 8/11/18, RT epochs 4/5/5.

E41.name: Maze size extrapolation: training on sizes 15–30 and testing up to 80
E41.protocol: Ten seeds each for HRM/RT, fixed final epoch-20 EMA; 12 sets of 1,000 mazes each; original 2D RoPE.

E42.name: SAT trained on 1,024 variables: four public subsets and internal long inference
E42.protocol: HRM raw step 61,440 and RT raw step 24,576; 219 train/108 validation/108 test instances; 864 public instances, K = 64 with 64–1,024 inference cycles; one internal trajectory through 16,384 inference cycles.

E43.name: Zero-shot graph coloring with SAT weights: 3-color, 4-color and Flat
E43.protocol: Reuses E42 HRM/RT weights, plus fixed QuerySAT/NeuroSAT weights; 1,000 graphs each for 3-color and 4-color, and 100 Flat graphs.

E44.name: CREMP DDPM HRM/RT/Ringer: augmentation×filtering
E44.protocol: Three models × with/without cyclic augmentation × three seeds = 18 fixed final non-EMA checkpoints at 20,000 updates; K = 64 and 20 DDPM steps.

E45.name: CREMP classical baseline: ETKDGv3 + MMFF94
E45.protocol: No neural checkpoint; three generation seeds; the same 256 validation molecules, with fixed energy and diversity filtering.

E46.name: Measured training time, per-instance latency and LLM API time
E46.protocol: One seed and final EMA for each of HRM/RT/shared-HL on Sudoku and Maze; separate SAT training records; LLM calls from E14.

E47.name: Training steps to peak performance: Easy versus standard
E47.protocol: Reuses ten standard HRM runs from E01 and three Easy HRM runs from E39; not 13 new training runs; means 48,533 versus 59,904.

E49.name: Trajectory recovery and local neighborhoods after L perturbations with fixed H
E49.protocol: The fixed-H trajectory case at H2/H3/H4; eight late states per phase × positive/negative .1 RMS perturbations = 16 branches, each continued for 4,096 L updates.

E50.name: Single-blank failures and first-H damping
E50.protocol: One frozen checkpoint; three pilot cases with 20 settings each; ten transfer cases from a 64-puzzle subset; known vulnerable cell 75; H1-only alpha .25/.5.

E51.name: Parameter counts, matrix FLOPs and computational budgets
E51.protocol: No additional trained weights; accounting must match each evaluated architecture configuration.
